title: Systemic Risk Bench: traditional-finance historical mechanism replays

coverage.scope: Selected crises and market-structure failures; not an exhaustive history or tick-level simulator.

shared_instructions: Evaluate evidence-linked decisions, risk decomposition, revision and self-critique; do not score exact crisis-name recall.
Require the agent to state horizon, units, loss sign, confidence level and probability measure before requesting CVA, settlement-loss or CVaR calculations.
Expose one stage at a time. Persist the previous answer and ask which assumptions changed, which action changed and why.
In the identity-masked track, remove case titles, dates, source links, proper nouns and distinctive historical magnitudes; test mechanism-preserving synthetic variants.
Use evaluator-only outcomes to assess reasoning, not to require foreknowledge. A defensible decision under the supplied information can differ from the realised outcome.
Every case should include adoption sweeps at fixed aggregate capital and at fixed capital per agent; do not mistake cohort count for market size.
shared_architecture_questions: Which reward, risk limit, memory horizon, state estimator or verifier assumption encourages this failure?
Would an independent risk critic actually see different evidence, or merely repeat the same model's premise?
What falsifiable test would cause the agent to abstain, reduce size, change execution or reject the strategy?
Which invariants can be formally checked, and which depend on market liquidity, legal enforceability or adversarial behaviour?
